criteria.evidence: The amendment adds no opcode or incompatible launch-0.9 argument tag. Its rejection of unchecked native-pointer casts is justified by §§4.1/7.1/10.
criteria.change: No score increase is available. Clarify §10: 'Registration capabilities are adapter values; after checked marshalling, ISA ptr values and ptrtoint/inttoptr retain their §§3.3/4.1 semantics. Integer conversion does not create a registration.'

criteria.evidence: Private coherent memory, no quantum-addressed native RAM reads, retained measurement/free restrictions and invocation-local reversal preserve the existing sound constructions. The import's position relative to reference execution should be explicit.
criteria.change: Add to §10: 'The imported image, mapping and metadata remain fixed throughout each coherent forward/inverse pair; replay is reversed before its preserved inputs are released, and private oracle writes are not published as native memory mutations.'

criteria.change: Add to §10: 'Host capture, registration and shim costs are reported separately; executed CC transfer instructions and quantum preparation, replay and cleanup retain their existing resource charges, and every replay row in the oracle reference body consumes one step of B.'

criteria.change: Add the consumer's three normative rows to 'Conformance vectors': repeated top calls produce '1 2 host_global=2'; an intervening g=40 produces '1 41 host_global=41'; top followed by another entry sharing g produces '1 2 host_global=2'.

criteria.change: Replace §0.3's ISA-11 classification with: 'Promotion retains the all-device construction; retaining pointer-sharing native callers requires the negotiated §10 mixed-memory contract and is a boundary capability obligation, not merely an efficiency improvement.'

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff — profile applicability, adapter descriptor and registration bindings; Conformance vectors

steps.claim: Mixed execution retains native callers, while genuinely shared globals retain one semantic identity. The consumer's dialect §4.3 explicitly says that clones share every global and that data is never cloned; ISA §12.3 requires the mixed-memory association and writeback contract.

The proposed diff requires the mixed profile for ordinary-pointer or aggregate calls, and describes positional arguments and registrations, but does not require implicit global dependencies to be registered or map each device global to its resolved native definition. Coordinating registrations already identified as shared does not establish that association.

The determining consumer fixture has @g = global i32 0 and a zero-argument top() that increments g. Its harness tests repeated calls, an intervening native write and a second marked entry. None requires a pointer or aggregate argument. The requested results are respectively '1 2 host_global=2', '1 41 host_global=41' and '1 2 host_global=2'. These fixture and harness sources were inspected; no new native integration execution is claimed.

The amendment supplies no mandatory descriptor association that makes this scalar-only entry use native g instead of its device layout image. Consequently, the central consumer blocker remains unanswered even though the rules for explicitly registered pointer arguments are improved.

blocking.fix: In §10, immediately after the adapter-descriptor paragraph, add: 'The descriptor MUST enumerate the selected device closure's boundary-shared global dependencies, including dependencies of entries with no pointer or aggregate arguments. Each binding associates a device program/global slot with the resolved native storage identity, extent and registration generation. All selected entries referring to the same native definition MUST bind the same canonical allocation; identical names or initial bytes alone do not establish identity. The native storage is authoritative: loading or unloading a device program MUST NOT reinitialize it. Before each CC/R invocation, current native bytes and required metadata are acquired under the lease, either through a live mapping or alias-preserving copy-in. Closing publishes the exact remaining prefix, and subsequent invocations observe intervening native edits. A device layout image is not a replacement for this binding.' Both coordinated live mapping and synchronized copy-in/writeback are viable; use copy-in/writeback as the minimal default bridge, with equivalent live mapping permitted. Add the three normative observation rows from step <1>3, including separate device entries sharing the same registration.

suggestions: Recommended exact spec diff, coherent-import paragraph: explicitly select the existing materialised replay construction as the default. State: 'Snapshot capture and CC register preparation occur before oracle entry; import/translation/replay instructions inside the oracle are reference-body rows, count against B, and enter source/closure identity. Direct initialization of private mem or alloctab from an invocation record is not authorized by this profile.' If direct imported-state initialization is preferred instead, amend §§3.7, 5.2, 11.1 and the invocation/certificate binding together. The distinction is observable: with g's image 00 and rows 'p = lift.addr @g; v = lift.load.i8 p; lift.retval v', B=3 returns payload 0/code 0. Changing the image to 09 returns 9/0 under a different identity. Inserting 'v = lift.const.i8 9; lift.store.i8 p v' after the address row returns 0/code 1 at B=3 and 9/code 0 at B=5. These results were checked through the reference interpreter using in-memory fixtures.

Hashes, catalog and consumers: add the full-version migration rule: 'Publishing ISA 0.10 changes version-prefixed symbol/interface/closure envelopes and object headers even when function bodies are unchanged. Regenerate affected object identities, downstream schedule/certificate bindings and consumer pins. ref@0.9 remains immutable; §17's version-relative default requires publication of the 0.10 catalog identity, or an explicit compatibility rule selecting an older catalog.' The current 219-recipe ref@0.9 catalog check passes with the published 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197 envelope hash; that does not establish a 0.10 catalog hash.

Recommended exact spec diff, synchronous-adapter paragraph: replace the unconditional result-extraction wording with: 'On COMPLETED, extract declared values and close before returning them. On FAILED, expose the terminal fault and no ordinary result values, then close with the retained-prefix policy. The default companion entry returns a tagged success/API-error/device-fault outcome; a source-ABI export binds an explicit failure continuation and MUST NOT manufacture a normal return value. A SUSPENDED run is resumed before bennett_wait is called again.' This makes the paragraph agree directly with §10's Results and Waiting rules.

Recommended exact spec diff, lease paragraph: clarify the relationship to §10's existing exclusive ownership rule: 'The registered read-only profile permits overlapping read leases only for storage and metadata that remain unchanged throughout those leases. Mutable registered storage retains exclusive ownership through CLOSED. This exception does not relax register-ledger ownership.'
path_to_accept: Add the mandatory implicit-global binding and authoritative native-state rules in NS1, then include the three exact consumer observation rows as conformance requirements. Numeric wire layouts and an implemented backend are not required for this proposal vote; their publication remains a prerequisite for consumer implementation.
summary: The boundary defect is real, the cited premises are accurate, and ISA 0.10 is the correct publication route. The core constructions remain sound. Revise the contract to bind implicit shared globals explicitly: pointer-argument registration alone does not resolve the live scalar-counter blocker.
